subject: Re: Service impact — proposed SLO compensation package for Orchid Health
messages:
From: Emily Zhang <emily.zhang@orchidhealth.com>
To: support@redwood.ai
Cc: contracts@orchidhealth.com
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 15:23:00 -0800
Subject: Latency spikes and request for compensation

Hi team,

We had significant latency spikes during our busiest window last Thursday (2026-11-05) that affected our patient intake flows. Our engineering team measured median response times from the Redwood API jumping from ~230ms to ~1.4s for ~45 minutes and we saw an increase in 5xxs correlated with the same window.

This caused a backlog in our ingestion pipeline and a measurable drop in throughput for that period. We're preparing a short incident timeline but wanted to start the conversation around compensation and a path to ensure this doesn't recur. Specifically:
- We expect a service credit to cover the extra costs we incurred in scaling fallback workers.
- We'd like assurance on steps you're taking to prevent recurrence (root cause + mitigation plan).

Can you confirm next steps and timing (we need something for our procurement team by next week)?

Thanks,
Emily
Emily Zhang
Director, Engineering Operations
Orchid Health

--
Attachment: orchid_slo_incident_report.pdf (summary, 3 pages)

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Latency spikes and request for compensation

Folks — forwarding Emily's note. Orchid is asking for a formal compensation package and a RCA/mitigation plan. I pulled the incident logs and the attached usage export; it looks like the 5xx spike coincided with a routing misconfiguration that caused a small percentage of traffic to land on an older model variant without KV cache priming. Jonas, can you confirm root cause and a short mitigation note for Emily?

Karthik/Marissa — quick ask: what's the maximum concession we can offer without needing exec signoff? Emily mentioned procurement wants numbers next week. I drafted a starter package in the attached spreadsheet (orchid_comp_package_v2.xlsx):
- Option A: $18,000 one-time usage credit + 1 month complimentary dedicated capacity at 25% off list for Nov
- Option B: $45,000 one-time credit (to offset added infra + third-party worker costs) + 2 months at 15% off

I think we should aim for A or a middle ground; if we go higher we'll need fast approval.

Vanessa
Director, Enterprise Sales Operations
Redwood Inference

--
Attachment: orchid_usage_nov_export.csv (500 lines, CSV excerpt)

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 17 Nov 2026 12:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Latency spikes and request for compensation

On Wed, Nov 11, 2026 at 09:15 AM Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Folks — forwarding Emily's note.

Root cause summary: a recent rollout included an old model shard mapping for a small subset of routes. The routing layer failed to prefer the primed pool due to a label mismatch during the rollout; the fallback behavior re-routed requests to a variant lacking warmed KV caches. We see ~3.7% of total requests affected during a 45-minute window, with the latency tail spiking and 5xxs at ~0.9% (baseline ~0.03%).

Mitigations already in place: forced rollback of the faulty mapping, corrected shard labels, and additional pre-deploy checks added to the rollout pipeline. We'll add a short automated smoke test to assert KV priming for any variant used in production within the next sprint.

Estimate of customer impact: based on Orchid's usage profile, the incremental infra and the cost of temporary fallback workers is roughly $22k. My recommendation: Option A with a small uplift to cover their third-party worker costs — say $25k + 1 month complimentary dedicated capacity at 20% off. This keeps it proportional and shows goodwill without setting a large precedent.

Jonas
Principal Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference

--
Attachment: (log excerpts inline)

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: CFO Execs <finance-approvals@redwood.ai>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 08:30:00 -0800
Subject: Executive approval request — Orchid Health compensation package (HB-8241)

Team,

Asking for rapid approval on a proposed compensation package for Orchid Health following a 45-minute routing incident that caused latency and 5xx spikes. Context: Jonas confirmed a routing-label regression; impact estimate is $22k incremental cost and customer operational pain. Procurement needs numbers this week.

Proposed offer (preferred):
- One-time usage credit: $25,000 (applied to outstanding/invoice balance)
- Service credit: additional $5,000 held in an escrow-like usage offset pool (applied over next 3 billing cycles as needed)
- Operational: 1 month complimentary dedicated capacity (technical uplift) at 20% off list rate

Total near-term P&L hit: ~$30k recognized as contra-revenue this quarter if approved. This is important to keep Orchid in the renewal motion — they're a fast-growing regional health platform with a multi-year intent and likely upsell.

If you approve, we'll finalize the exact language with Legal and send a joint note to Emily + Contracts. If you need different accounting treatment (credit vs. refund), let me know.

Approve: Reply ALL with APPROVE and any redlines. If rejected, advise a maximum allowable concession and I will communicate.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Director, Enterprise Sales Operations
Redwood Inference

--
Attachment: orchid_comp_package_v2.xlsx (proposed options)

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Zhang <emily.zhang@orchidhealth.com>, contracts@orchidhealth.com
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 22 Nov 2026 10:10:00 -0800
Subject: Proposed remediation & compensation for 2026-11-05 incident (HB-8241)

Emily / Contracts team — thank you for your patience while we investigated. Attached is our RCA and proposed compensation package. Summary of our offer: 

- One-time usage credit of $25,000 to be applied to your next invoice.
- $5,000 service offset held as a three-month usage pool that can be applied automatically if you see higher-than-expected infra spend tied to fallback workers.
- 1 month of complimentary dedicated capacity for November with a 20% concession on list dedicated rates (to help with momentary capacity and to validate routing stability).

Jonas has included the mitigation steps in the RCA. Short version: a rollout label mismatch sent ~3.7% of traffic to a variant without warmed caches; we've corrected the mapping, tightened rollout checks, and added an automated smoke test to validate KV priming during deploys.

If this package looks acceptable, please confirm and we will have Legal draft a short amendment and apply the credit. If you'd like a different split of credit vs. escrow, we're open to a quick call to finalize.

Apologies again for the disruption — we value the partnership and want to make this right.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Director, Enterprise Sales Operations
Redwood Inference

--
Attachments: orchid_slo_incident_report.pdf, orchid_comp_package_v2.xlsx
